name: sqlite3WhereBegin
prose: Builds the code-generation plan and the VDBE loop code for a WHERE clause over pTabList and returns a newly allocated WhereInfo (the return at sqlite3.c:171765, after the codegen loop at 171718-171760), or returns a null pointer in the failure cases below. Return 0 at 171182: pTabList->nSrc is greater than BMS; it raises the error "at most %d tables in a join" through sqlite3ErrorMsg first, and no WhereInfo has been allocated yet. All other failures go to the label whereBeginError (171768), which, if pWInfo is non-null, restores pParse->nQueryLoop from pWInfo->savedNQueryLoop, frees it with whereInfoFree and returns 0. The gotos are: db->mallocFailed after the WhereInfo allocation (171204, where pWInfo is freed and set to 0 first, so only the return remains), pParse->nErr after the WHERE-term analysis (171295), a nonzero rc from whereLoopAddAll (171383, 171402), db->mallocFailed after wherePathSolver (171408, 171412), pParse->nErr after the optimiser stage (171430), db->mallocFailed before the code-generation loop (171712), and pParse->nErr or db->mallocFailed inside the loop (171722, 171749). On success the caller owns the WhereInfo, which is meant to be released by sqlite3WhereEnd.
note: [R:right] reviewer says allocation failure is recorded in db->mallocFailed rather than pParse->nErr: yes (171203-171204), and the old failure-case list was incomplete (missed 171383/171402/171408/171412/171430/171712/171722/171749). Slice cut the head; function is at 171130-171779. Read: head, all return/goto lines and the error label; the middle loop-planning and per-level code (171433-171705) read only by return/goto scan, not line by line.

name: sqlite3_test_control
prose: Variadic dispatcher for the SQLITE_TESTCTRL_* test hooks (this slice covers the part of the function starting inside its switch). In a build with SQLITE_UNTESTABLE it does nothing and returns 0 (186793-186794, 187355-187356). Otherwise it reads the extra arguments for op with va_arg (types must match what the chosen case reads), runs that case, and then returns rc at the single return at 187356. rc starts at 0 (186792) and is set only by these cases: BITVEC_TEST (the result of sqlite3BitvecBuiltinTest, 186884), FAULT_INSTALL (sqlite3FaultSim(0), 186910), PENDING_BYTE (the PENDING_BYTE value, 186943), ASSERT (the int argument x, 186967; x stays 0 if assert is compiled out), ALWAYS (ALWAYS(x) when x is nonzero, else 0, 187024), BYTEORDER (SQLITE_BYTEORDER*100 + SQLITE_LITTLEENDIAN*10 + SQLITE_BIGENDIAN, 187040), ISINIT (SQLITE_ERROR when sqlite3GlobalConfig.isInit is 0, 187174), PARSER_COVERAGE (SQLITE_ERROR when sqlite3ParserCoverage(out) is nonzero, 187222, only when YYCOVERAGE is defined) and TUNE (SQLITE_NOTFOUND when id is 0 or outside plus or minus SQLITE_NTUNE, 187326, only when SQLITE_DEBUG is defined and SQLITE_OMIT_WSD is not). There is no default case, so an unrecognized op also leaves rc at 0. IMPOSTER holds db->mutex while it looks up the schema name and updates db->init, and leaves the mutex before break (187197-187207). SEEK_COUNT writes sqlite3BtreeSeekCount of the main database to *pn (187255).
note: [R:right] reviewer: omits ALWAYS and BYTEORDER return values / rc not only OK/ERROR - right (rc set at 186884-187326 by nine cases) and the old prose wrongly claimed SQLITE_NOTFOUND for an unrecognized op (no default case, 187353). Partly read: the bodies of PRNG_*, FK_NO_ACTION, BENIGN_MALLOC_HOOKS, OPTIMIZATIONS, GETOPT, LOCALTIME_FAULT, INTERNAL_FUNCTIONS, NEVER_CORRUPT, EXTRA_SCHEMA_CHECKS, ONCE_RESET_THRESHOLD, VDBE_COVERAGE, SORTER_MMAP, TRACEFLAGS, LOGEST were only checked for rc assignments (none) and not read for their side effects. Whole function is 186791-187357.

name: sqlite3_test_control
prose: Variadic dispatcher for the SQLITE_TESTCTRL_* test hooks (this slice covers the tail of the function, from TRACEFLAGS to the end). In a build with SQLITE_UNTESTABLE it does nothing and returns 0. Otherwise it reads the arguments for the chosen op with va_arg, runs the matching case and returns rc at the single return (187356). rc starts at 0 and is changed only by BITVEC_TEST, FAULT_INSTALL, PENDING_BYTE, ASSERT, ALWAYS, BYTEORDER, ISINIT, PARSER_COVERAGE (when YYCOVERAGE is defined) and TUNE; no other case assigns it, and there is no default case, so an unrecognized op returns 0. In this tail: RESULT_INTREAL calls sqlite3ResultIntReal on the sqlite3_context argument (187238-187239) and keeps rc; SEEK_COUNT stores sqlite3BtreeSeekCount(db->aDb->pBt) in *pn (187255); TUNE writes Tuning(id) from *piValue for 0<id<=SQLITE_NTUNE, writes *piValue from Tuning(-id) for -SQLITE_NTUNE<=id<0, and otherwise sets rc to SQLITE_NOTFOUND (187321-187326); these TUNE and JSON_SELFCHECK bodies exist only when SQLITE_DEBUG is defined and SQLITE_OMIT_WSD is not, and JSON_SELFCHECK with those options reads *pOnOff and either stores the current bJsonSelfcheck into it when it is negative, or sets bJsonSelfcheck to its low 8 bits (187344-187349); without them it does nothing.
note: [R:right] reviewer: JSON_SELFCHECK does not always write through its pointer - right (187345-187349: only the negative case writes *pOnOff, otherwise it only reads). Old prose's "rc NOTFOUND for unrecognized op" was also wrong (no default case). TRACEFLAGS and LOGEST (187269-187317) read only by rc scan, not for their writes. Whole function 186791-187357.

name: sqlite3Fts3MsrCancel
prose: If pExpr->bEof is nonzero on entry, returns SQLITE_OK without touching pExpr (194872, 194880). Otherwise it saves pExpr->iDocid, calls fts3EvalRestart, and then, while rc is SQLITE_OK and pExpr->iDocid differs from the saved value, calls fts3EvalNextRow and sets rc to FTS_CORRUPT_VTAB whenever pExpr->bEof is set after that call (194873-194878). That check runs after each advance, so FTS_CORRUPT_VTAB is returned if the end is reached on an advance even if the docid then happens to equal the saved one, and the result is also an error code from fts3EvalRestart or fts3EvalNextRow if they report one. It returns SQLITE_OK when the loop exits with rc unchanged, which includes when restart already leaves iDocid equal to the saved value. The single return is at 194880.
note: [R:right] reviewers: (1) bEof already set returns OK (194872) right; (2) FTS_CORRUPT_VTAB after bEof even if iDocid equals saved - right (194877 sets it inside the loop after each advance, unconditionally on bEof). Function is at 194870-194881; read in full.

name: sqlite3Fts3EvalPhrasePoslist
prose: Looks up the position list of phrase pExpr for column iCol in the current row and stores a pointer into *ppOut; *ppOut is set to 0 at 195118 before anything else. It returns SQLITE_OK with *ppOut still 0 when the phrase is restricted to a different column (195120-195121), when the phrase is not below an OR node while its docid does not match pCsr->iPrevId or it is at EOF (195147), when no position list is found (195218), or when the column list ends before iCol is reached (195228). If pExpr->iDocid equals pCsr->iPrevId and pExpr->bEof is zero, the phrase's current doclist pointer is used directly. Otherwise, for a phrase below an OR node it takes the nearest non-deferred ancestor pRun of the topmost NEAR ancestor pNear (or of pExpr itself when it has no NEAR ancestor), and, if pPhrase->bIncr is set, restarts pRun and advances it until it reaches the saved docid or hits EOF (195157-195168); if any ancestor was at EOF it advances pRun to EOF (195169-195173). Errors from fts3EvalRestart/fts3EvalNextRow are returned (195174), and FTS_CORRUPT_VTAB is returned when pRun->bEof differs from its value before the restart (195165-195167). It then scans the phrases in the NEAR chain, moving each one's cached OR poslist/docid until it reaches pCsr->iPrevId, and uses its own cached poslist only if every phrase matches that docid (195176-195216). Finally it skips column lists until it reaches iCol and sets *ppOut to the list only if the column found equals iCol, else 0 (195226-195237).
note: [R:right] reviewer: FTS_CORRUPT_VTAB can also occur when pNear is the phrase itself - right (pNear starts as pExpr, 195141, and pRun is derived from it, so the 195165 check applies without a NEAR ancestor). Function is at 195104-195238; read in full, pPhrase assignment at 195110 not displayed (not needed).

name: sqlite3Fts3Incrmerge
prose: Performs incremental merging on the FTS3 table p, with a work quota nMerge (leaf pages to write) and a minimum segment count nMin that is raised to at least 2 in the level query (204395). It allocates one block holding the cursor, filter and writer and returns SQLITE_NOMEM if that fails (204377). Otherwise it loads the merge hint from the %_stat table and loops while rc is SQLITE_OK and nRem is positive (204382). Each pass finds the absolute level with the smallest number of segments that is at least MAX(2,nMin) via SQL_FIND_MERGE_LEVEL, optionally replaces it with the next entry popped from the hint when no such level exists or the hint's level is not later in the level order (204415-204426), and leaves the loop if the resulting segment count nSeg is not positive (204437). It returns FTS_CORRUPT_VTAB if the level number is negative or above nMod<<32 (204440-204442). Otherwise it merges the oldest nSeg segments of that level into one segment using the incremental writer, subtracts the pages written plus one from nRem, and records the remaining segments in the hint (204499-204505). A SegReaderStep result that is neither SQLITE_OK nor SQLITE_ROW finishes the cursor, leaves the loop and is returned (204476-204478). The loop ends without error when nRem is exhausted or no level qualifies; running out of hint entries alone does not end it. After the loop it writes the hint back to %_stat if it was changed and rc is SQLITE_OK (204522-204523), frees the block and the hint buffer, and returns rc (204526-204528); on errors rc is the first error code recorded by the helpers, which are not individually read here.
note: [R:right] reviewers: (1) pnRem annotation: no such parameter - right, old prose mentions none now; (2) hint exhaustion alone does not stop the loop - right (only nSeg<=0 at 204437 or an error or nRem<=0 ends it). Function is at 204363-204529; read in full, but the helper functions (fts3Incrmerge* , SegReader*) are not read, so "first error code" is stated generally.

name: jsonErrorFunc
prose: Generated SQL function json_error_position(X) (the scalar function jsonErrorFunc, argc==1). Builds a JsonParse s with s.db set to the connection (212538-212539). If argv[0] is a JSONB blob (jsonArgIsJsonb) the result value is whatever jsonbValidityCheck(&s,0,s.nBlob,1) returns. Otherwise it takes the text of argv[0] via sqlite3_value_text; if that is NULL (an SQL NULL argument or an out-of-memory failure) the function returns at once without setting a result and without calling jsonParseReset (212543-212544). Otherwise it converts the text to JSONB with jsonConvertTextToBlob: if that succeeds the position stays 0; if it fails with s.oom set the position becomes -1, and if it fails otherwise the position is one plus the number of non-UTF-8-continuation bytes among the first s.iErr bytes of the text, i.e. a 1-based character offset (212546-212557). After that it calls jsonParseReset(&s) and sets the SQL result with sqlite3_result_error_nomem when the position is negative, else with sqlite3_result_int64 of the position (212560-212564).
note: [R:n/a] still-rejected only for "name not in slice"; the slice (212536-212793) starts inside this function, the real definition is jsonErrorFunc at 212528-212566, not jsonErrorPosition (no such function exists). Fixed under the real name; slice cut the head. Read in full; jsonbValidityCheck and jsonConvertTextToBlob not read.

name: rtreeBestIndex
prose: xBestIndex for the R-Tree virtual table. It first scans all constraints, including unusable ones, and sets bMatch if any has op SQLITE_INDEX_CONSTRAINT_MATCH (215500-215504); that scan is complete before the second loop begins, so a MATCH constraint that comes later in the array also sets bMatch. In the second loop, if bMatch is 0 and a constraint is usable, has iColumn<=0 and op SQLITE_INDEX_CONSTRAINT_EQ (a rowid lookup), it clears argvIndex and omit for all earlier constraints, sets idxNum=1, argvIndex=1 and omit=1 for that constraint, sets estimatedCost=30.0, estimatedRows=1 and idxFlags=SQLITE_INDEX_SCAN_UNIQUE, and returns SQLITE_OK at once (215510-215532). Otherwise a usable constraint on a coordinate column (1<=iColumn<=nDim2) or a usable MATCH constraint with op EQ, GT, LE, LT, GE or MATCH appends two characters (the operator and the column digit) to zIdxStr, sets its argvIndex to the running count and sets omit to 0 for EQ, GT and LT and to 1 for LE, GE and MATCH (215535-215555); other ops are skipped. The loop stops early when the local zIdxStr buffer is full (215507). After the loop it sets idxNum=2 and needToFreeIdxStr=1, and when iIdx>0 allocates idxStr with sqlite3_malloc and returns SQLITE_NOMEM if that fails (215559-215566); otherwise it copies the string, sets estimatedRows to pRtree->nRowEst >> (iIdx/2) and estimatedCost to 6.0 times that, and returns rc, which is SQLITE_OK as initialised (215573).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: strategy 1 can trigger before a later MATCH; bMatch only tracks earlier constraints - wrong: bMatch is set by a full pass over every constraint at 215500-215504 before the loop at 215507 starts, so a later MATCH already disables strategy 1. Slice cut the head; function at 215485-215574, read in full.

name: rbuSetupCheckpoint
prose: Void helper that prepares an RBU handle for the checkpoint stage, working through p->rc and p->eStage. If pState is NULL it first sets p->eStage to 0, even if p->rc is already an error, and when p->rc is SQLITE_OK it runs "SELECT * FROM sqlite_schema" on p->dbMain and stores the result in p->rc (224308-224313). If p->rc is SQLITE_OK it then sets p->eStage to RBU_STAGE_CAPTURE and runs "PRAGMA main.wal_checkpoint=restart"; its result goes into p->rc unless it is SQLITE_NOTICE, which is ignored (224343-224348). If p->rc is still SQLITE_OK and p->nFrame>0 it sets p->eStage to RBU_STAGE_CKPT, p->nStep to pState->nRow (or 0 when pState is NULL), allocates p->aBuf of p->pgsz bytes with rbuMalloc, and sets p->iWalCksum from rbuShmChecksum (224350-224355). If p->rc is still SQLITE_OK after that, then when p->nFrame is 0, or pState is non-NULL and its iWalCksum differs from p->iWalCksum, it sets p->rc to SQLITE_DONE and p->eStage to RBU_STAGE_DONE; otherwise it computes p->nPagePerSector from the target file's sector size (at least 1) and calls xSync on the WAL file, storing the result in p->rc (224357-224378). With an earlier error in p->rc and a non-NULL pState nothing is changed. On a failure in the checkpoint step eStage can stay RBU_STAGE_CAPTURE, and p->iWalCksum is not set when nFrame is 0.
note: [R:right] reviewers: (1) on error eStage can remain CAPTURE/0 and iWalCksum is unset when nFrame==0 - right (224345 sets CAPTURE before the checkpoint; 224354 only inside nFrame>0); (2) with p->rc not OK and pState NULL it still sets eStage=0 - right (224309 runs before the rc test). Function at 224303-224380, read in full; rbuMalloc, rbuShmChecksum not read.

name: rbuMoveOalFile
prose: Void helper for the MOVE stage of an RBU update; asserts p->eStage is RBU_STAGE_MOVE and p->rc is SQLITE_OK with p->zErrmsg zero (224531-224532). It builds the names "<f>-oal" and "<f>-wal", where f is the main database filename of p->dbMain, or of p->dbRbu when rbuIsVacuum(p) (224520-224529). If either allocation fails it sets p->rc to SQLITE_NOMEM, sets no error message, and leaves the connections and files alone (224533-224534). Otherwise it applies rbuFileSuffix3 to both names, finalizes the object iterator, closes p->dbRbu and p->dbMain and sets both pointers to 0 (224544-224552). It then opens a new handle on p->zTarget with rbuOpenDbhandle and, if that returned a handle, takes its lock with rbuLockDatabase, storing the result in p->rc (224554-224558). If p->rc is SQLITE_OK it renames oal to wal with p->xRename (224560-224562); a rename is therefore attempted even when no handle was opened as long as p->rc is still OK. The new handle is closed and cleared if p->rc is an error, or the update is a vacuum, or rbuExclusiveCheckpoint(dbMain)==0 (224564-224570). If p->rc is OK it then calls rbuOpenDatabase(p, dbMain, 0) and rbuSetupCheckpoint(p, 0) (224572-224575). Both name strings are freed on every path (224578-224579).
note: [R:right] reviewers: (1) on allocation failure only rc=NOMEM, no zErrmsg, and rename/reopen do not always occur - right (224533-224534, 224560, 224572); (2) a vacuum closes the handle - right (224565). Function at 224519-224580, read in full; rbuOpenDbhandle, rbuLockDatabase, rbuExclusiveCheckpoint not read.

name: sqlite3rbu_step
prose: Performs one unit of work for an RBU handle and returns p->rc, or SQLITE_NOMEM when p is NULL (224968, 225085-225087). It switches on p->eStage. RBU_STAGE_OAL: for a vacuum with p->nProgress==0 and p->rc OK it first creates the target schema and copies user_version and application_id (224975-224979). It then loops over the object iterator while p->rc is SQLITE_OK: for an iterator in cleanup state it deletes the rbu_tmp table rows when the update is not a vacuum and pIter->abIndexed is set; otherwise it prepares the statements, steps the SELECT, and if a row was returned increments p->nProgress and p->nStep and returns rbuStep(p) directly (224981-225001); if no row was returned it resets the SELECT into p->rc and sets p->nStep to 0, and the iterator advances (225003-225008). The cleanup and table-advance paths do not increment nProgress. When the loop ends with p->rc OK it saves the state with RBU_STAGE_MOVE, increments the schema cookie, commits on dbMain and dbRbu while rc stays OK, and sets eStage to RBU_STAGE_MOVE (225011-225021). RBU_STAGE_MOVE: if p->rc is OK it calls rbuMoveOalFile and increments p->nProgress (225027-225029). RBU_STAGE_CKPT: if p->rc is OK, when p->nStep>=p->nFrame it syncs the target file, maps shared memory and writes p->iMaxFrame to word 24, and on success sets eStage to RBU_STAGE_DONE and p->rc to SQLITE_DONE (225036-225054); otherwise it checkpoints frames one sector at a time (225066-225075); nProgress is incremented after either branch (225077). Other stages do nothing. The return value is the p->rc held at that point.
note: [R:right] reviewers: nProgress can increment without eStage advancing, and OAL cleanup/table-advance paths do not increment nProgress - both right (225077, 225029 versus 224981-225008). Function is at 224967-225089 (the slice cut the head; first lookup landed on a different function). Read in full; rbuStep, rbuCheckpointFrame, rbuSaveState and others not read.

name: fts5yy_reduce
prose: Parser-generated reduce step of the FTS5 query grammar parser (Lemon). The slice cuts the head; the function starts at 237523. It starts from the stack top fts5yymsp = fts5yypParser->fts5yytos (237537), then runs the semantic action of rule fts5yyruleno through a large switch (for example case 0 calls sqlite3Fts5ParseFinished(pParse, ...) at 237551; the default case does nothing, 237690-237691). After the switch it takes the rule's left-hand-side symbol fts5yygoto from fts5yyRuleInfoLhs and fts5yysize from fts5yyRuleInfoNRhs, which is zero or a negative number (minus the length of the right-hand side), looks up the new state with fts5yy_find_reduce_action on the state found fts5yysize entries below the top (237695-237697), moves the local pointer by fts5yysize+1 entries, stores it back into fts5yypParser->fts5yytos, sets that entry's stateno and major to the new state and the left-hand-side symbol, traces the shift, and returns the new state (237706-237711). The effect on the stack is that the right-hand-side entries are replaced by one entry (it is not an explicit destroy of each popped entry apart from whatever the rule action itself does), and for an empty right-hand side the stack grows by one entry. The function does not check stack room itself; sqlite3Fts5Parser grows the stack before calling it for a rule whose right-hand side is empty. It has a single return, at 237711.
note: [R:mixed] reviewers: (1) advances stack pointer by size+1 rather than popping RHS entries - code does add fts5yysize+1 (237706), but fts5yysize is the negative RHS length so this moves the top back over the RHS, which is the pop, then pushes the LHS entry; reviewer partly right that nothing is destroyed here. (2) precondition treats NRhs as positive - right, fts5yyRuleInfoNRhs holds zero or negative values (237696 used as an index offset). Read: head, tail (237690-237712) and the case table only by grep, not the individual reduction actions (237539-237691).

name: sqlite3Fts5Parser
prose: Feeds one token (fts5yymajor, fts5yyminor; major 0 means end of input) to the FTS5 expression parser fts5yyp, a Lemon-generated driver, and returns nothing; it processes only this token, not a whole input. It loops: it finds the action for the token in the current state (237843); if that is a reduce, then for a rule with an empty right-hand side it first grows the stack when the top is at the stack end and, if growing fails, calls fts5yyStackOverflow and leaves the loop (237867-237880), then calls fts5yy_reduce and loops again with the returned action (237882); if it is a shift (or shift-reduce), it calls fts5yy_shift and leaves the loop (237883-237888); if it is the accept action, it pops the top, calls fts5yy_accept and returns immediately (237889-237892); any other action is a syntax error. In this file fts5YYNOERRORRECOVERY is defined (sqlite3.c:236557) and no error symbol is defined, so the compiled error branch is the NOERRORRECOVERY one, which calls fts5yy_syntax_error, destroys the token and leaves the loop (237959-237969); the other error branches (error-symbol recovery at 237904 and the default one at 237970-237991, which calls fts5yy_parse_failed at end of input) are compiled out here. The error counter is not touched in this configuration (237885-237887 are compiled out). When it leaves the loop it prints the stack in debug builds and returns (237995-238007).
note: [R:right] reviewers: (1) only processes a single token, not until accept/end of input - right (one pass of the while(1) loop per call, breaks at 237878/237888/237969); (2) syntax-error path conditional, annotation omits error-symbol shifting and parse_failed in default branch - right, but those branches are compiled out given 236557. Function at 237804-238008, read in full except the debug trace code; fts5yy_shift/fts5yy_find_shift_action not read.

name: fts5MultiIterNew
prose: Builds a multi-segment iterator over an FTS5 index and stores it in *ppOut; it returns nothing and reports problems through p->rc. The slice cuts the head; the function starts at 248148. It asserts that either pTerm==0 and nTerm==0, or iLevel<0 (248164), so a non-NULL pTerm is expected only when iLevel<0. If p->rc is SQLITE_OK it counts the segments: for iLevel<0 all pStruct->nSegment segments plus one for the in-memory hash when p->pHash is set and FTS5INDEX_QUERY_SKIPHASH is not in flags, otherwise MIN(nSeg of that level, nSegment) (248167-248174). It always assigns *ppOut = fts5MultiIterAlloc(p, nSeg) (248176); if that is NULL it goes to the end label, leaving *ppOut 0 (the assert at 248178 expects p->rc to be an error). Otherwise it copies bRev, bSkipEmpty and pColset from flags and arguments and sets the output callback unless FTS5INDEX_QUERY_NOOUTPUT is set (248181-248186). If p->rc is still OK it initializes one segment iterator for the hash (if counted) and one for every segment of every level (a term seek when pTerm is non-NULL), or for the first nSeg segments of the named level in reverse order, and asserts that iIter equals nSeg (248189-248214). If p->rc is still OK after that it calls fts5MultiIterFinishSetup; otherwise it frees the new iterator and sets *ppOut to 0 (248221-248226). At the end label the assert says *ppOut is non-NULL or p->rc is an error (248229).
note: [R:right] reviewer: precondition reversed; iLevel<0 may have non-NULL pTerm, the assert only requires pTerm==0 && nTerm==0 when iLevel>=0 - right (248164). Slice cut the head; function at 248148-248231, read in full; fts5MultiIterAlloc, the SegIter init helpers and FinishSetup not read.

name: fts5StorageDeleteFromIndex
prose: Removes the index contributions of row iDel in an FTS5 storage object. It asserts bSaveRow is 0 or 1 and that bSaveRow is 1 only with apVal==0 (258102-258103), so with bSaveRow==0 apVal may be NULL or point to the row's nCol values. If apVal is NULL it reads the row through a statement: when bSaveRow is set and p->pSavedRow exists it takes over that saved statement (258107-258109); otherwise it gets the lookup statement, binds iDel and steps; if there is no row it returns sqlite3_reset(pSeek) without any change to totals (258111-258116), and a failure to get the statement is returned at 258112. Then for each column that is not marked unindexed it takes the value (from the statement row or from apVal), decodes the locale value or copies a non-text value, and tokenizes the text with sqlite3Fts5Tokenize and fts5StorageInsertCallback (258139-258166). After each column it subtracts the counted size ctx.szCol from p->aTotalSize and sets rc to FTS5_CORRUPT if the total went negative while rc was SQLITE_OK (258167-258170). After the loop, if rc is OK and p->nTotalRow<1 it sets rc to FTS5_CORRUPT, and otherwise it decrements p->nTotalRow by one, which also happens when rc already held an error (258176-258180). Finally, if rc is OK and bSaveRow is set, the statement is stored in p->pSavedRow without being reset; otherwise the statement is reset and its result becomes rc if rc was OK (258182-258188). The result is returned at 258189.
note: [R:right] reviewers: (1) nTotalRow decremented by one, absent row returns OK without writes - right (258179, 258114-258115); (2) apVal need not be non-NULL when bSaveRow==0 - right (258106 handles NULL). Function at 258089-258190, read in full; fts5StorageInsertCallback, sqlite3Fts5Tokenize not read.

name: afpLock
prose: Lock method for the AFP (Apple Filing Protocol) VFS: tries to raise the file's lock level to eFileLock. If pFile->eFileLock is already at least eFileLock it returns SQLITE_OK at once, before taking the inode mutex (41810-41814). Otherwise it asserts the lock order (a first lock must be SHARED, the requested level is not PENDING, RESERVED is requested only from SHARED; asserts only, 41821-41823), enters pInode->pLockMutex (41828) and leaves it on every path before returning (41964). Returns SQLITE_BUSY without changing any lock state when another unixFile on the inode holds a different level and either the inode is at PENDING or above or a level above SHARED is requested (41833-41837). A SHARED request when the inode already holds SHARED or RESERVED just records the SHARED level in pFile and increments pInode->nShared and nLock (41844-41852). Otherwise, for a SHARED request, or an EXCLUSIVE request from below PENDING, it first takes the PENDING byte lock through afpSetLock, and returns the failure code if that fails (41859-41867). For a SHARED request it then locks a random shared byte, releases the PENDING byte, returns the first error code from either step if one is a lock error, or the busy-style code from the shared-byte lock without recording the lock, and on success sets pFile->eFileLock to SHARED, nShared to 1 and increments nLock (41873-41906). An EXCLUSIVE request with pInode->nShared>1 gives SQLITE_BUSY (41907-41910). name: winLock
prose: Win32 VFS lock method: tries to raise the lock level of pFile (a winFile) to locktype. It returns SQLITE_OK immediately if pFile->locktype is already at least locktype (50664-50666), and SQLITE_IOERR_LOCK if the file is read-only (WINFILE_RDONLY) and locktype is RESERVED_LOCK or higher (50671-50672). For a SHARED request, or an EXCLUSIVE request made from RESERVED, it tries to lock the PENDING byte with LockFileEx up to three times, sleeping 1 ms between failed attempts, and returns SQLITE_IOERR_LOCK immediately (without changing pFile->locktype) if the failure is ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE (50686-50725). With the pending byte held (or not needed) it then, depending on locktype: acquires the shared lock by winGetReadLock and records SHARED (50730-50742); locks the RESERVED byte and records RESERVED (50746-50754); for EXCLUSIVE sets the recorded level to PENDING_LOCK (this happens even when the request started at SHARED and no pending byte was locked, 50758-50760) and then unlocks the shared lock, locks the whole shared range, records EXCLUSIVE on success, or tries to re-take the shared lock on failure (50765-50776). A pending byte taken for a SHARED request is released again (50781-50783). At the end it returns SQLITE_OK if the last step succeeded (res nonzero), otherwise it stores the last error in pFile->lastErrno and returns SQLITE_BUSY; in both cases pFile->locktype is set to the new level reached so far, which can be SHARED, RESERVED or PENDING_LOCK after a failed request (50788-50799).

prose: Appends the super-journal (master journal) name record to the rollback journal file; the packet name pager_write_superjournal does not exist, the function is writeSuperJournal (sqlite3.c:59760-59823; the slice cut the head). prose: Ends the current write transaction of a pager; the real function is pager_end_transaction at 60097-60225 (slice cut the head). If pPager->eState is below PAGER_WRITER_LOCKED and pPager->eLock is below RESERVED_LOCK it returns SQLITE_OK at once and does nothing (60116-60118). Otherwise it releases all savepoints and, if the journal file is open, finishes the journal according to its mode: an in-memory journal is closed; truncate mode truncates to 0 when journalOff is nonzero and syncs it when fullSync is set, then sets journalOff to 0; persist mode, or exclusive mode below WAL, calls zeroJournalHdr and sets journalOff to 0; any other mode closes the journal and deletes the journal file with sqlite3OsDelete only when the pager is not a temp file (60124-60167), the result going into rc. It then frees pInJournal and clears nRec (60181-60183). If rc is SQLITE_OK it cleans all dirty pages when the database is in memory or flush-on-commit applies and otherwise clears their writable flags, and truncates the page cache to dbSize (60184-60191). With WAL it calls sqlite3WalEndWriteTransaction into rc2 (asserted to be SQLITE_OK, 60198-60199); without WAL, on commit when rc is OK and the file is longer than dbSize, it truncates the file (60200-60209). If rc is OK and bCommit is set it sends SQLITE_FCNTL_COMMIT_PHASETWO and treats SQLITE_NOTFOUND as success (60211-60214). If the pager is not in exclusive mode (and, for WAL, sqlite3WalExclusiveMode(...,0) is true) it drops to a SHARED lock with pagerUnlockDb, storing the result in rc2 (60216-60220). It sets eState to PAGER_READER and setSuper to 0 and returns rc if rc is not SQLITE_OK, else rc2 (60221-60224).

prose: Reads one record (page number and page image) from the main journal or a sub-journal and writes the page back to the database file and/or the page cache; the function is at sqlite3.c:60343-60545 (slice cut the head). It reads the page number and the page data from the journal at *pOffset and returns the error code of either read at once (60382-60385); after a successful read it advances *pOffset by the page size plus 4 (plus 4 more for the main journal checksum, 60386). It returns SQLITE_DONE without playing back if pgno is 0 or the super-journal marker page number (60393-60395); returns SQLITE_OK without playing back if pgno is beyond pPager->dbSize or its bit is already set in pDone (60397-60399); for the main journal it reads the checksum and returns the read error, or SQLITE_DONE if the checksum of a non-savepoint record does not match (60400-60405). prose: Writes a list of dirty pages (linked through pDirty) to the database file; defined at sqlite3.c:62470-62551. prose: First phase of a commit: syncs the journal and writes the dirty pages, or writes them to the WAL; defined at sqlite3.c:64506-64725. prose: Reads the wal-index header into pWal->hdr, running recovery if the header is invalid; defined at sqlite3.c:68518-68621 (slice cut the head). prose: Opens a B-tree on a database file (or temp or memory database) and stores the new Btree in *ppBtree; defined at sqlite3.c:74081-74374 (slice cut the head). It computes isTempDb (no filename) and isMemdb (":memory:", an in-memory temp database or SQLITE_OPEN_MEMORY), sets BTREE_MEMORY in flags for a memory database, and turns a main-database open of a temp or memory database into a temp-database open (74097-74126). For a shareable database (shared-cache flag, not temp) it builds the full pathname (failure other than SQLITE_OK_SYMLINK is returned after freeing p and the name; an allocation failure returns SQLITE_NOMEM_BKPT) takes the open mutex and the shared-cache list mutex, and searches the shared list for a BtShared on the same file and VFS; if the same BtShared is already used by another database of this connection it returns SQLITE_CONSTRAINT after leaving the mutexes and freeing p (74143-74198), otherwise it reuses the match and increments nRef (74191-74192). If shareable it then links the new Btree into the per-connection sorted sibling list (74316-74340) and stores p in *ppBtree (74342). At btree_open_out, if rc is not SQLITE_OK it closes the pager if one exists, frees pBt and p, and sets *ppBtree to 0 (74345-74351); if rc is SQLITE_OK it sets the cache size to SQLITE_DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE only when sqlite3BtreeSchema(p,0,0)==0 and sends SQLITE_FCNTL_PDB only when the pager file has methods (74359-74366). name: sqlite3BtreeSetAutoVacuum
prose: Sets the auto-vacuum mode of the B-tree database; defined at sqlite3.c:74746-74764 (slice cut the head). With SQLITE_OMIT_AUTOVACUUM compiled in it just returns SQLITE_READONLY (74747-74748). Otherwise it narrows autoVacuum to an 8-bit value av (so, for example, 256 behaves as 0) (74752), enters the Btree, and if the page size is already fixed (BTS_PAGESIZE_FIXED) and av is nonzero in a way that differs from the current pBt->autoVacuum setting (compared as 0 or 1) it sets rc to SQLITE_READONLY and changes nothing (74755-74756). Otherwise it sets pBt->autoVacuum to 1 if av is nonzero (else 0) and pBt->incrVacuum to 1 only when av equals 2 (74758-74759). name: btreeBeginTrans
prose: Begins a read (wrflag==0) or write (wrflag>0; wrflag==2 asks for an exclusive transaction) transaction on the B-tree; defined at sqlite3.c:75142-75324 (slice cut the head). Under the Btree mutex it first jumps to trans_begun if p is already in a write transaction, or in a read transaction with a read request (75158). It returns SQLITE_READONLY if the database is read-only and a write is requested (75170-75173; the SQLITE_ResetDatabase flag can first clear the read-only flag); with shared cache it returns SQLITE_LOCKED_SHAREDCACHE (and notes the blocking connection) when another connection holds a write transaction or a pending lock, or when an exclusive transaction is asked for and another Btree holds a lock (75182-75199); it returns the error of querySharedCacheTableLock if the schema-table read lock is refused (75206-75207). Otherwise it loops: it calls lockBtree until page 1 is loaded, for a write it calls sqlite3PagerBegin and newDatabase (a SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT with no transaction open becomes SQLITE_BUSY), and on any error it releases the WAL write lock and unlocks the Btree if unused; the loop repeats while the code is a busy code, the shared Btree has no transaction and the busy handler asks to retry (75211-75261). If rc is SQLITE_OK it records the transaction in p->inTrans and pBt->inTransaction (and the shared-cache lock list and pWriter for a write), and, if the header's database size differs from pBt->nPage, makes page 1 writable and stores the size (75267-75303); that sqlite3PagerWrite can fail after inTrans was already set (75279, 75299), in which case the error is returned although the transaction state has been recorded. At trans_begun, when rc is SQLITE_OK it stores the schema cookie in *pSchemaVersion if given and, for a write, opens the savepoints with sqlite3PagerOpenSavepoint (75307-75318); then it leaves the Btree and returns rc (75322-75323).

name: sqlite3BtreeTableMoveto
prose: Moves cursor pCur on an integer-key table B-tree to the entry with key intKey, or to where it would be, and reports the comparison in *pRes; defined at sqlite3.c:77293-77434 (slice cut the head). Fast path: if the cursor is valid with a valid cached key, then an equal key gives *pRes=0 and SQLITE_OK at once (77310-77312), a cursor already at the last entry with a smaller key gives *pRes=-1 and SQLITE_OK (77315-77318), and a key exactly one larger than the cached one sets *pRes=0, calls sqlite3BtreeNext and returns SQLITE_OK if the new key equals intKey or the error if it is not SQLITE_DONE (77324-77334); otherwise it falls through. These early returns do not reset pCur->info.nSize. The general path calls moveToRoot: SQLITE_EMPTY gives *pRes=-1 and SQLITE_OK, other errors are returned (77343-77350). It then binary-searches each page, starting at the middle or, with biasRight, the last cell; a corrupt cell varint returns SQLITE_CORRUPT_PAGE (77382-77384). An exact match on a leaf sets ix, the cached key (flag BTCF_ValidNKey), info.nSize=0 and *pRes=0 and returns SQLITE_OK (77394-77405); an exact match on an interior page and any non-exact interior page descend to the child at lwr with moveToChild (77420-77428). A leaf with no match stores the position and *pRes=-1 or +1 with rc SQLITE_OK and goes to the finish label (77413-77418). At moveto_table_finish (reached by a leaf miss or by a moveToChild error) it sets info.nSize to 0 and returns rc (77430-77433).

name: fillInCell
prose: Builds the on-page image of one B-tree cell in pCell from the payload description pX, and stores its size in *pnSize; the real name is fillInCell (static, sqlite3.c:78560-78743), not the unnamed name in the packet, and the slice cut the head. The header starts with childPtrSize bytes, followed for an integer-key leaf by the payload size varint (nData+nZero) and the key varint, or for an index cell by the key-length varint (78585-78598). If the payload fits (nPayload<=maxLocal) it copies nSrc bytes, zero-fills the rest of the payload, sets *pnSize to header plus payload but at least 4 (writing a zero byte into the cell when it is shorter), and returns SQLITE_OK (78602-78617). Otherwise it computes the local size n from minLocal and usableSize, sets *pnSize to n+header+4 and copies the payload piece by piece (78623-78629): the local part into the cell, then, for each full chunk, it allocates an overflow page with allocateBtreePage (taking the next non-pointer-map, non-pending-byte page number when auto-vacuum is on), records it in the pointer map for auto-vacuum databases, writes the page number into the previous page or into the 4 bytes after the local payload, and continues on the new page with usableSize-4 bytes of space; source bytes missing beyond nSrc are written as zeros (78659-78738). If allocateBtreePage or ptrmapPut fails it releases the page it held and returns that error code, leaving the cell partly written (78698-78720). Otherwise it releases the last overflow page and returns SQLITE_OK (78741-78742).

The old prose also said it always returns SQLITE_OK, which is wrong because of the error return at 78720. Read in full; allocateBtreePage and ptrmapPut not read.

name: sqlite3_backup_step
prose: Copies up to nPage pages (all remaining pages when nPage is negative) from the source to the destination database of backup object p; defined at sqlite3.c:83380-83632 (slice cut the head). It returns SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT at once if p is NULL (83387). Otherwise it enters the source database mutex, the source Btree and, if p->pDestDb is non-NULL, the destination database mutex (83389-83393), and releases the same three before its single exit (83626-83631). It reads rc from p->rc and does the work only if that is not fatal; isFatalError treats SQLITE_OK, SQLITE_BUSY and SQLITE_LOCKED as non-fatal (83283-83285, 83396); a fatal stored code is returned again without further work. In the work part it returns SQLITE_BUSY if the destination is a separate connection and the source has a write transaction (83406-83407), opens a read transaction on the source if none is open (closing it again at the end), sets the destination page size, takes a write transaction on the destination and records the schema cookie (83416-83437), and sets SQLITE_READONLY if the destination is in WAL mode or in memory and the page sizes differ (83444-83449). It then copies pages with backupOnePage in a loop that stops on the first error (83456-83467); on success it sets nPagecount and nRemaining and returns SQLITE_DONE if all pages were copied, otherwise attaches the backup object if needed (83468-83475). On SQLITE_DONE it updates the destination meta data, resets the destination schemas, sets the WAL version if needed, truncates or rewrites the destination file as needed for the page sizes, commits the destination, and sets rc to SQLITE_DONE only if everything succeeded (83483-83606). Any other code is carried through. It ends the source read transaction if it opened it, maps SQLITE_IOERR_NOMEM to SQLITE_NOMEM_BKPT, and stores rc in p->rc (83614-83624); so SQLITE_OK, SQLITE_BUSY and SQLITE_LOCKED results are also stored but are not treated as fatal by later calls, while other errors are returned again by every later call.

name: sqlite3VdbeNextOpcode
prose: Finds the next opcode to list, for the EXPLAIN and bytecode-listing code, and returns it through *paOp and *piAddr, with *piPc advanced; defined at sqlite3.c:88153-88257 (slice cut the head). It sets nRow to the main program's opcode count plus the opcode counts of the sub-programs already collected in the blob pSub (88176-88187). It then advances a row counter from *piPc: when the counter reaches nRow it sets p->rc to SQLITE_OK and returns SQLITE_DONE (88191-88194); otherwise it selects the opcode from p->aOp or from the sub-program that holds that row (88196-88211). If pSub is non-NULL and the opcode has a sub-program operand not yet recorded, it grows pSub with sqlite3VdbeMemGrow, appends the sub-program and adds its opcode count to nRow; if growing fails it stores that code in p->rc and returns SQLITE_ERROR (88219-88236). Which opcodes stop the scan depends on eMode: for 0 every opcode; for 1 only OP_Explain, or OP_Init when it is not the first row (88249-88250); the eMode 2 test (stop at OP_OpenRead, OP_OpenWrite without P2ISREG, OP_ReopenIdx) exists only when SQLITE_ENABLE_BYTECODE_VTAB is defined (88239-88245), and other values of eMode are not handled in a build without it (there an assert requires eMode==1, 88248). Before returning it stores the advanced counter in *piPc and the row index, the program array in *piAddr and *paOp, and returns rc (88253-88256).

name: vdbeCommit
prose: Commits all write transactions of connection db; the packet name sqlite3VdbeCommit does not exist, the function is the static vdbeCommit at sqlite3.c:88810-89062 (slice cut the head). It first runs sqlite3VtabSync (88831), then scans the databases: for each one in a write transaction it notes that a commit is needed, counts it in nTrans if its synchronous level is not OFF, its journal mode needs a super-journal (DELETE, PERSIST or TRUNCATE) and it is not an in-memory pager, and takes an exclusive pager lock; the scan stops at the first non-OK code, which is returned (88839-88869). If a commit hook is set and a commit is needed it calls the hook and returns SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_COMMITHOOK when the hook returns nonzero (88873-88877). If the main database has no filename or nTrans is at most 1, it runs sqlite3BtreeCommitPhaseOne on every database, then, if all succeeded, sqlite3BtreeCommitPhaseTwo on each, and calls sqlite3VtabCommit if rc is SQLITE_OK (88889-88912). Otherwise (multi-file transaction) it builds a unique super-journal name next to the main file (SQLITE_NOMEM_BKPT if that allocation fails), retrying up to 100 times when the name exists, creates it exclusively, writes the journal name of each database in a write transaction, syncs it unless the device is sequential, runs phase one with the super-journal name on every database, closes it, and deletes it, which is the commit point (88931-89033). On an error before the delete it frees the name and returns the error (after closing and deleting the file once it was open, 88963-89002, 89023-89025); a failed final delete is returned (89035-89036). On success it runs phase two on all databases ignoring their result, then calls sqlite3VtabCommit (89046-89057). The function returns rc at 89061, which is SQLITE_OK in the multi-file success case.
